content.title: BIGBANG Electrifies Coachella Debut With 17 Hits
content.text: On the 12th, local time, the group Big Bang showcases their 20th-anniversary debut stage at the U.S. 'Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival'. They state, 'It is truly meaningful that we have spent more than half of our lives together as members, as Big Bang.' /Screenshot from YouTube‘The Mysterious Explosion That Marked the Beginning of the Universe’. The idol group BIGBANG made a striking debut in August 2006, leaving a powerful first impression on the Korean music industry. This year, marking their 20th anniversary since debut, they took the stage at the ‘Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival’ (hereafter Coachella) held in Indio, California, U.S.At 10:40 p.m. local time on the 12th, G-Dragon (real name Kwon Ji-yong, 38 years old), Daesung (37 years old), and Taeyang (real name Dong Young-bae, 37 years old) appeared alongside a video of an exploding universe, fitting the group’s name. From their first song, “Bang Bang Bang,” the trio electrified the audience with their live performance skills. After the song, G-Dragon shouted BIGBANG’s signature group cheer, “B to the I to the G to the bangbang,” prompting the audience to erupt in cheers of “oppa” in Korean.This performance was BIGBANG’s first Coachella appearance and a headline act for their 20th anniversary, drawing significant attention. It was the final slot at the festival’s prominent ‘Outdoor Theater’ venue. The Coachella YouTube channel, with 5.85 million subscribers, saw multinational fans leaving comments like “King of K-pop” and “Banchella” (BIGBANG + Coachella) from an hour before the live stream began, eagerly anticipating the group’s appearance.In response, BIGBANG delivered 17 hit songs over approximately one hour, rearranged in diverse styles. From EDM pop (“Fantastic Baby,” “Good Boy”), R&B (“Day by Day,” “Lie”), reggae (“Bad Boy”), to funk (“We Like to Party”), BIGBANG’s mid-2000s hits transformed into various genres as if they were new releases. The performance underscored their status as the ‘original’ idol group with in-house production capabilities, beyond just singing and dancing.Even G-Dragon, who recently faced controversy over vocal issues during a solo concert, showcased stable harmonies alongside Daesung and Taeyang, both renowned for their vocal prowess.There was also a ‘surprise twist’ in the setlist: Daesung’s solo trot songs “Han-do Cho-gwa” (2025) and “Look at Me, Defect” (2008). As the rock guitar and drums, which had been playing sleek funk, abruptly shifted to a flirtatious 4/4 beat, the Coachella venue erupted in explosive cheers. It marked the first time trot music was performed at Coachella and the most Korean-centric stage yet.On the 12th, local time, Big Bang's Daesung showcases his solo trot song 'Look at Me, Defect' with a cute dance routine at the U.S. 'Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival'. The audience erupts in laughter as Daesung cheekily introduces the song in English, shouting, 'She who seeks to "rock with me" and defect!' /Screenshot from YouTubeThe grand finale was “Spring Summer Fall Winter (Still Life)” (2022). Although BIGBANG originally had five members, Victory left the group after retiring from the entertainment industry amid the ‘Burning Sun scandal,’ and T.O.P also departed following this song. However, during the performance, the members played a pre-recorded vocal of T.O.P, creating the illusion of singing together. Before leaving the stage, G-Dragon shouted in Korean, “Please look forward to our fun 20th-anniversary adult ceremony soon!” eliciting roaring cheers.Coachella, running from the 10th to the 19th of this month, is the largest music festival in the U.S., attracting 200,000 to 300,000 attendees. This year, alongside BIGBANG, various K-pop artists graced the lineup. On the 11th, TAEYIN became the first Korean male solo artist to perform solo, and on the 10th, the group HUNTR/X (EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami), part of “KPop Demon Hunters,” joined the K-pop collaboration group KATSEYE for a joint performance of “Golden.” BIGBANG will take the Coachella stage once more on the 19th.On the 12th, local time, the group Big Bang showcases their 20th-anniversary debut stage at the U.S. 'Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival'.
